clue.text: Top cover for retirement

parts.note: a cap is a covering for the top of the head, and retirement is going to bed; the clue also hints at a last drink before bed

explanation.surface: Sounds like insurance or a roof over a pensioner's head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retirement' looks like leaving work, but here it means retiring to bed for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the cap traditionally worn in bed, so it covers the head when one goes to sleep.

clue.text: Pet about to be given American food

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
a noodle is a kind of food made from pasta dough

explanation.surface: A pet animal is fed something American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like a noun for an animal but is the verb meaning to cuddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To canoodle is to kiss and cuddle amorously, which is what petting means as a verb.

clue.text: A theologian to finish article, they are found at the end

definitions.text: they are found at the end

parts.note: DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, a theologian's degree
to end something is to finish it
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A theologian completes an essay whose extras are appended at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: Addenda are supplementary items added at the close of a book or document.

clue.text: Break hole in wall

definitions.meaning: a ... is a pause or break, as in a school or parliamentary ...
an alcove or niche set back into a wall

explanation.surface: Someone smashes a gap in a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both an interval in proceedings and an indentation or niche in masonry.

clue.text: Collect maybe where light gets in through

indicators.note: the beam of light gets into the word for through, so it sits inside it

parts.note: per means through or by means of, as in per post
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: Someone describes a spot where daylight enters a room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collect' looks like a verb but is the noun: a short prayer said in church services.
explanation.definitionFit: A collect is a brief liturgical prayer, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Gradient Brian negotiated having to grit his teeth

indicators.note: the two words have been worked through and rearranged, as a route is negotiated

explanation.surface: Brian tackles a steep hill and has to endure it.
explanation.definitionFit: To grin and bear it is to endure hardship stoically, much as one clenches one's jaw.

clue.text: Travelling extensively running after the ball

indicators.note: the word for running is placed after the word for the ball

parts.note: the globe is the ball of the Earth
trotting is running at a gentle pace

explanation.surface: A player is chasing the ball across the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Globetrotting means touring the world widely, which is travel on a grand scale.

clue.text: Carry coffee from French filling station

parts.note: to transport is to carry
café is the French word for coffee

explanation.surface: Someone takes French coffee away from a petrol station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling station' looks like a petrol station, but here it is a place where people get filled up with food; a transport café is a cheap British roadside diner for lorry drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside diner is a stop where drivers fill their stomachs, a humorous twist on fuelling.

clue.text: After sound of disapproval, who heard sound of weeping?

indicators.note: the second part comes after the sound of disapproval

parts.note: boo is a jeer of disapproval

indicators.note: heard says the word who is to be taken by how it is spoken

parts.note: who is pronounced hoo

explanation.surface: After the jeering, someone asks who is heard crying.
explanation.definitionFit: Boo-hoo imitates loud sobbing or blubbering.

clue.text: Ordinary to be occurring seven times a week

definitions.text: to be occurring seven times a week

explanation.surface: Something routine is said to happen daily.
explanation.definitionFit: Commonplace things are routine, and a daily event recurs on all seven days.

clue.text: Have no credit in old money

indicators.note: no says the credit abbreviation is taken away

parts.note: a crown was a pre-decimal British coin worth five shillings

explanation.surface: Someone is broke, without credit, in pre-decimal days.
explanation.walkthrough: A crown was an old British coin, worth a quarter of a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to have or possess it.

clue.text: Guarded, having received stolen goods

definitions.meaning: enclosed or protected by a fence
to fence is to handle stolen goods, so this is the past tense of that slang sense

explanation.surface: A suspect is under guard after handling stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A fenced area is protected by a barrier; a fence is also a dealer in stolen property.

clue.text: Daughter and I emphasise pain

parts.note: to stress something is to emphasise it

explanation.surface: A parent says that she and her daughter stress how much it hurts.
explanation.definitionFit: Distress is suffering or anguish, a synonym for pain.

clue.text: Drink with three-quarters of side

indicators.note: three-quarters of says one of the four letters of the word for side is dropped, here its final one

parts.note: a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A drink comes with a portion of a side dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side' looks like a side dish, but it is a sports team; the first three of its four letters are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is a hot drink brewed from leaves.

clue.text: Support the new visionary

parts.note: a prop is a support

indicators.note: new says the letters of the word the are made afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: An endorsement for the latest seer.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophet is a seer who foresees the future, i.e. one with visions.

clue.text: Husband has two opposing points to axe

parts.note: E and W, east and west, are opposite points of the compass

explanation.surface: A husband has two contrary arguments for firing someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'points' are compass points here, not arguments.
explanation.definitionFit: To hew is to chop with an axe or similar blade.

clue.text: Ghost said supporter will accompany cat

indicators.note: said says the word for supporter is taken as spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: a fan is a supporter
a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A spooky tale of a fan and a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: A phantom is a spectre or apparition.

clue.text: Companion giving friendly assistance?

definitions.meaning: a companion or partner, especially a spouse
the question mark flags the playful reading

explanation.surface: A partner who lends a hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A helpmate is a supportive partner, and read in two parts it means aiding a pal.

clue.text: Turned into nice poisonous alkaloid!

indicators.note: turned says the letters of the next words are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Something pleasant has become a toxin.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicotine is the toxic alkaloid found in tobacco.

clue.text: Deputy has most of the reputation

indicators.note: most of says the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: standing is one's reputation or status

explanation.surface: A deputy enjoys much of the boss's prestige.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in is a substitute who takes someone's place.

clue.text: Firm breaking law in the beginning

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters go inside the word for the beginning

parts.note: the start is the beginning

indicators.note: breaking says the word law is broken up and its letters reordered

explanation.surface: A company was breaking the law from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' rearranges LAW into ALW, which goes into START.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalwart means steadfast, loyal and unwavering, just as firm does.

clue.text: Instruction to players to take it smoothly

definitions.text: Instruction to players to take it smoothly

parts.words: Instruction to players to take it smoothly
parts.note: players are musicians, and the musical direction meaning play smoothly and connected is meant

explanation.surface: Sounds like a coach calming down a sports team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'players' looks like sportsmen, but they are musicians reading a score.
explanation.definitionFit: Legato is the Italian musical direction to play notes smoothly with no break between them.

clue.text: Real upset about politician is more considerable

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go around the politician
upset says the word real is knocked over into a new order

parts.note: MP stands for Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A genuinely upset politician seems a bigger deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges REAL into ALER, which goes 'about' MP.
explanation.definitionFit: Ampler means larger or more plentiful, i.e. greater in size or amount.

clue.text: Find a colt rampaging with energy

indicators.note: rampaging says the young horse runs wild, so its letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Track down a young horse running wild with vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: To locate something is to discover where it is.

clue.text: Cleopatra's poisoner found within?

indicators.note: found within says the answer lies inside the run of letters of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A whodunnit asking whether the Egyptian queen's killer was an insider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found within' signals letters hidden across the end of CLEOPATRA'S and the start of POISONER; the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says the Egyptian queen killed herself with the bite of this venomous snake.

clue.text: Section of drawing spanning width

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a technical drawing covers its full breadth.
explanation.definitionFit: A wingspan is the distance from wingtip to wingtip, the breadth of a bird or aircraft.

clue.text: Given and received from building society perhaps

definitions.meaning: shared or reciprocated, felt by each party towards the other
a member-owned financial institution, such as a British building society (a savings and mortgage lender)

explanation.surface: Something passed back and forth with a savings society.
explanation.definitionFit: Reciprocal feelings pass both ways; a British building society is a member-owned savings lender.

clue.text: Last to end of boxing match, or race?

definitions.text: Last to end of boxing match, or race?

parts.words: Last to end of boxing match, or race?
parts.note: last means survive: a boxer who survives every round, or a runner who completes the course

explanation.surface: Asks who came last at the end of a fight or race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' looks like finishing at the back, but it is the verb meaning endure.
explanation.definitionFit: To go the distance is to keep going to the finish, surviving all rounds or the full course.
